requirements.businessContext: The Auction Marketplace lets teams in Complete-tier auction leagues trade rostered players and cash between themselves, or release players back into the mini-auction pool. Every accepted P2P trade requires a final admin approval, and superadmins also hold direct override tools (force-approve / force-reject / cancel) plus low-level corrections (undo-sale, manual-transfer) for auction results. The marketplace is locked while a live auction session is running, and pending proposals are purged when a session begins.

userStories.iWant: to propose a player + cash trade to another team in my league
userStories.soThat: I can restructure my squad outside of auction sessions

userStories.iWant: to accept or reject an incoming trade proposal
userStories.soThat: I control which trades happen to my squad

userStories.iWant: to see all my outgoing and incoming proposals, and (separately) league-wide live offers excluding my own
userStories.soThat: I can monitor open negotiations and discover deals others are publicising

userStories.iWant: any pending proposal I leave untouched to expire after 24 hours
userStories.soThat: the marketplace does not fill up with stale offers

userStories.iWant: to approve an accepted trade so players, cash, and the 5% transfer fee actually move
userStories.soThat: I am the final gatekeeper before economy state changes

userStories.iWant: to reject a pending or accepted trade outright (force-reject)
userStories.soThat: I can block trades I judge collusive or illegal
I can clear the queue when an auction session is about to start or after a dispute

userStories.iWant: to mark a player for release
userStories.soThat: I recover purse at the next GW10/20/30 boundary and let the player return to the mini-auction pool

userStories.iWant: to cancel a pending release I no longer want
userStories.soThat: I keep the player on my active roster

userStories.iWant: to undo a mistakenly sold auction bid
userStories.soThat: I can correct admin errors that produced a wrong sale

userStories.iWant: to manually move a player to another team (or back to the unowned pool) with a custom price
userStories.soThat: I can fix ownership errors without unwinding a full auction session

userStories.iWant: to purge every pending/accepted trade the moment a live auction session starts
userStories.soThat: stale proposals cannot execute against squads that are about to change

businessRules.rule: Trade endpoints require a valid team session. POST /api/auction/trade and PATCH /api/auction/trade return 401 'Team authentication required' for guest or superadmin sessions.
POST /api/auction/trade requires non-empty `leagueId` and `targetTeamId` in the body — missing either returns 400.
A team cannot propose a trade to itself: when `session.id === targetTeamId` the server returns 400 'Cannot trade with yourself'.
Trades are restricted to leagues with `format = 'auction'`. Any other format returns 400 'Not an auction league'.

POST and PATCH on /api/auction/trade gate trade operations by requiring leagues.auctionTier === 'complete'. Any other value (including 'primary', null, unset, or any future tier name) returns 403 'Trades are only available in Complete tier'. Allow-list (not deny-list) approach so adding a new tier defaults to denied.
Marketplace is closed during a live auction: if `isAuctionLive(leagueId)` returns true, POST and PATCH return 409 'Marketplace is closed during a live auction'.

Every offered ownership ID must belong to the proposer (`auctionOwnership.teamId === session.id`); every requested ownership ID must belong to the target. Mismatch returns 400 with the offending player's name.

Only ownership rows with `status = 'active'` are eligible. Released or pending_release ownerships are silently excluded by `buildTradePlayers` and will surface later as a 'don't own player' validation error.
Trade validity is enforced by `validateTradeProposal`: post-trade squad size must stay between 11 and `effectiveMaxSquadSize(penaltySlots, bonusSlots)` on both sides.
Post-trade position quotas must be respected on both sides: at least 1 GK, 3 DEF, 3 MID, 1 FWD remaining. When position data is available, violations return per-side per-position error messages.
Cash check: if `cashOffered > 0` the proposer must have enough purse; if `cashOffered < 0` the target must have enough purse. Insufficient purse on either side fails validation.

FMV floor: each side must give at least 80% of the total FMV it receives (FMV math defined in module 11). Floors are computed as `Math.floor(otherSideGivesValue * 0.8)` and undervaluation produces a 'Trade undervalues what X gives' error.
A proposal must involve at least one player on at least one side — cash-only trades (offered=[] and requested=[]) are rejected with 'Trade must involve at least one player'.

On successful POST the proposal is written to `tradeProposals` with `status='pending'`, the provided cashOffered (default 0), JSON-stringified player ID arrays, and server-generated `id` + timestamps.

On POST success a `trade_proposed` notification is created for the target team only. Body uses the proposer's PL Club Auction rename when present, else the team's name, else 'A team'. The link deeplinks to `<leagueSlug>/marketplace?tab=incoming`.
Lazy expiry: every GET and every PATCH first marks any pending proposal whose `createdAt` is older than 24h as `expired` before doing anything else.
PATCH /api/auction/trade requires `proposalId` and `action ∈ {'accept','reject'}`. Any other action value returns 400.

PATCH requires the proposal to be in `status='pending'`. Already accepted/rejected/cancelled/completed/expired proposals return 400 'Proposal is no longer pending'. Stale-pending proposals past 24h return 410 'Proposal expired (24h limit)'.
Only the target team can respond to a proposal — `session.id !== proposal.targetTeamId` returns 403 'Only the target team can respond'.

On `reject` the proposal moves to `status='rejected'`, `updatedAt` is bumped, and a single `trade_rejected` notification is sent to the proposer using the target's club/team display name and a `tab=outgoing` deeplink.

On `accept` the server re-runs `validateTradeProposal` against fresh squad/purse/penalty/bonus data and returns 400 'Trade is no longer valid' if validation now fails — accepting a stale proposal cannot execute the trade.

On `accept` success the proposal moves to `status='accepted'` and a `trade_accepted` notification with body '<target> accepted your trade — awaiting admin approval' is sent to the proposer. Players and cash do NOT move yet — they move only after admin approval.

The peer-veto system has been removed. /api/auction/trade/veto returns HTTP 410 Gone unconditionally. GET /api/auction/trade response does NOT expose vetoDeadline or vetoVotes. The tradeProposals.vetoDeadline + tradeProposals.vetoVotes columns remain in the schema for backwards compatibility with existing rows but are deprecated; new code must not write to them.

POST /api/auction/trade/admin accepts: (a) superadmin sessions on any league, OR (b) admin sessions that hold a leagueAdmins row for the proposal's leagueId. Anyone else (team session / anonymous) gets HTTP 403. The proposal is loaded first so its leagueId is known when scoping admins.
Admin actions accepted: `action ∈ {'approve','reject','cancel'}`. Any other value (or missing proposalId) returns 400.
Admin `approve` is only allowed when `proposal.status === 'accepted'`. Pending/rejected/cancelled/expired/completed proposals return 400 with the current status echoed back.

Before executing the trade the admin path re-validates squad sizes, purses, penalty/bonus slots, and position quotas with `validateTradeProposal`. If validation fails the trade is NOT executed and 400 'Trade is no longer valid' is returned.

`executeTrade` runs as a single DB transaction: all offered ownerships are reassigned to the target, all requested ownerships to the proposer, cash + 5% transfer fee is applied, and the proposal is marked `status='completed'`. Partial failures roll the whole thing back.

Cash transfer applies a 5% transfer fee to the recipient: when `cashOffered > 0` the proposer's purse drops by the gross amount and totalSpent rises by the gross; the target's purse rises by `gross - round(gross * 0.05)` and totalIncome rises by the same net. When `cashOffered < 0` the roles flip. (The 5% rate definition lives in module 11; module 12 covers WHEN it is applied — at admin approval.)
On admin `approve` success both proposer and target receive a `trade_approved` notification with body 'Admin approved the trade — players & cash have been transferred' and a `tab=history` deeplink.
Admin `reject` is allowed only when current status is `pending` or `accepted`; sets `status='rejected'`, bumps `updatedAt`, and sends both parties a `trade_admin_rejected` notification.

Admin `cancel` is allowed for any proposal that is NOT `completed`; sets `status='cancelled'` and sends both parties a `trade_cancelled` notification. Cancelling a completed trade returns 400 'Cannot cancel a completed trade'.
POST /api/auction/release accepts either a team session (owning the player) or a superadmin. Anonymous callers receive 401.
POST /api/auction/release requires `ownershipId`. Missing returns 400, unknown ID returns 404, league not in `auction` format returns 400 'Not an auction league'.

Release moves the ownership from `status='active'` to `status='pending_release'` only. Players already `released` return 400 'Player is already released'; players already `pending_release` return 400 'Player is already marked for release'. Purse and totalRefunds are NOT credited yet — the actual refund finalises at GW10/20/30 boundaries.
Release response returns a *projected* refund computed via `calculateRefund(purchasePrice)` (50% of purchase price) for display only, plus the projected forfeit (the other 50%).
DELETE /api/auction/release reverts a pending-release ownership back to `status='active'`. Calling DELETE on a row that is not `pending_release` returns 400 'Player is not pending release'.

Both POST and DELETE on /api/auction/release require leagues.auctionTier === 'complete' (allow-list). Any other tier (primary, null, future tiers) returns HTTP 403 with body containing 'Releases are only available in Complete tier'. Mirrors the trade-route pattern (BR-TRADE-005).

POST /api/auction/release does NOT check `isAuctionLive(leagueId)` before flipping the ownership status. // CODE-CONFIRMED: may be a defect — the trade endpoint blocks during a live auction (BR-TRADE-006) but release does not, so a team can mark a player for release mid-auction, which `purgePendingTrades` does not handle. Confirm with product owner.

The auth shape of /api/auction/trade/admin now matches /api/admin/[leagueId]/auction-corrections: both accept superadmin + assigned league admin. League admins of an active league have parity between low-level corrections (undo-sale, manual-transfer) and trade-admin actions (approve / reject / cancel).
`action='undo-sale'` requires `bidId` in the body. The bid must exist (404 otherwise) and must be in `status='sold'` (400 'Bid is not in sold status' otherwise).

Undo-sale finds the matching active `auctionOwnership` row (by leagueId + fplElementId), deletes it, refunds the buyer by decrementing `teams.totalSpent` by `ownership.purchasePrice`, and marks the bid `status='cancelled'`. All of this happens inside a single DB transaction.

Undo-sale and manual-transfer adjust BOTH `teams.totalSpent` AND `teams.purse` inside the existing db.transaction so the team's spendable cash stays consistent with the ledger after a correction. Undo-sale credits the buyer's purse by the purchasePrice as totalSpent decrements. Manual-transfer to unowned credits the original owner's purse by the purchasePrice. Manual-transfer cross-team credits the original owner's purse by purchasePrice and debits the new owner's purse by transferPrice (with new owner's totalSpent incremented).
`action='manual-transfer'` requires `ownershipId` and `toTeamId`. Missing either returns 400; unknown ownership returns 404 'Ownership not found'.
Manual-transfer with `toTeamId === 'unowned'` deletes the ownership row and credits `teams.totalSpent` back to the original owner (decrement by purchasePrice).

Manual-transfer with a real `toTeamId` reassigns the ownership row to the new team, sets `purchasePrice` to the supplied `price` (falling back to the existing price), refunds the original owner's totalSpent, and charges the new owner's totalSpent — all within a transaction.
Any unknown `action` value returns 400 'Unknown action' with no DB writes.

When a league's auction session transitions to active, `purgePendingTrades(leagueId)` flips every `pending` or `accepted` proposal in that league to `status='cancelled'` in one bulk update and returns the count purged. (Detailed handling lives in module 10; module 12 records this as the trigger that clears the marketplace.)

GET /api/auction/trade supports three modes selected by query params: (a) `scope=public` returns league-wide live offers — only `pending` or `accepted` proposals, and for team sessions excludes proposals where the caller is the proposer or the target; (b) `teamId=...` returns proposals where that team is proposer OR target; (c) no params returns every proposal in the league.

The tradeProposals.status enum no longer emits 'vetoed'. Active platform code produces only 'pending', 'accepted', 'rejected', and 'expired'. Historical rows with status='vetoed' remain visible via GET (no migration), but no new row will ever land on that value.

Notification triggers WHAT (not UI rendering — UI is module 15): a successful POST fires `trade_proposed` to the target; a successful PATCH `accept` fires `trade_accepted` to the proposer; a successful PATCH `reject` fires `trade_rejected` to the proposer; admin `approve` fires `trade_approved` to both parties; admin `reject` fires `trade_admin_rejected` to both parties; admin `cancel` fires `trade_cancelled` to both parties.

`tradeProposals.status` lifecycle observed in code: `pending` → (team accepts → `accepted` | team rejects → `rejected` | 24h passes → `expired`); `accepted` → (admin approves → `completed` | admin rejects → `rejected` | admin cancels → `cancelled`); `pending` can also be admin-cancelled or admin-rejected. Bulk-cancel by `purgePendingTrades` flips `pending`/`accepted` → `cancelled`. The legacy `vetoed` value defined in the schema is no longer produced anywhere.

defects.title: Trade tier gate matches 'not primary' instead of 'complete only'
defects.description: Both POST and PATCH on /api/auction/trade gate trades by checking `leagues.auctionTier === 'primary'`. The product brief specifies trades as Complete-tier ONLY. The current code therefore allows trades on any tier other than 'primary' — if a third tier is added (or `auctionTier` is null/unset/typoed), trades would silently be enabled.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Allow trades only when `auctionTier === 'complete'`. Any other value (including null, primary, or future tiers) should return 403.
defects.actualBehaviour: Any tier that is not literally the string 'primary' lets trades through.
defects.notes: Low risk today because only 'primary' and 'complete' tier values exist, but trivially exploitable if a new tier label is introduced or a migration leaves the column null. Fix: switch to explicit allowlist `auctionTier === 'complete'`. [DEV] Self-verified: cleanup-only fix; no behaviour change. [QA-VERIFIED] Inverted pinning TC(s). [BA-UPDATED] BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: Both POST (line 134-137) and PATCH (line 308-313) tier gates in src/app/api/auction/trade/route.ts now allow-list 'complete' instead of denying 'primary'. A future third tier, plus null / unset / typo'd auctionTier values, defaults to denied — closing the silent-allow loophole.

defects.title: /api/auction/release lacks a tier gate (Primary tier can release players)
defects.description: POST /api/auction/release never reads `leagues.auctionTier`. According to the module 12 scope brief, marketplace features (including releases) are Complete-tier ONLY. The trade endpoint enforces this server-side; the release endpoint does not.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Return 403 'Releases are not available in Primary tier' when `leagues.auctionTier === 'primary'` (mirror BR-TRADE-005).
defects.actualBehaviour: A Primary-tier team can flip any of its players to pending_release through this endpoint, which would later forfeit purse at the GW10/20/30 boundary in a tier that should not support releases at all.
defects.notes: Direct economy impact at the next refund boundary. Fix: add the same `auctionTier === 'primary'` (or 'complete' allowlist) check the trade route uses. defects.resolution: Added a Complete-tier allowlist gate to both POST and DELETE handlers in src/app/api/auction/release/route.ts. POST gates after the auction-league check (route.ts:63-65); DELETE now also fetches leagueRow and gates after the ownership-of-player check (route.ts:137-144). Both return 403 { error: 'Releases are only available in Complete tier' } when leagueRow[0].auctionTier !== 'complete', mirroring the canonical pattern in src/app/api/auction/trade/route.ts:138 (post DEF-TRADE-001). Allow-listing 'complete' (rather than denying 'primary') ensures any future tier label, plus null / unset values, defaults to denied.

defects.title: /api/auction/release is not blocked during a live auction session
defects.description: The trade endpoint refuses to operate while `isAuctionLive(leagueId)` is true. The release endpoint never calls isAuctionLive at all, so a team can flip any of its players to pending_release while the auction is in progress. `purgePendingTrades` clears proposals when a session starts but does not undo or block in-flight releases.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Return 409 'Marketplace is closed during a live auction' (same as BR-TRADE-006) when there is an active or paused session for the league.
defects.actualBehaviour: Release proceeds during a live auction; the player remains scoring for the team until the next GW boundary, but the marketplace was supposed to be closed.
defects.notes: Inconsistency with the trade path. Fix: add `if (await isAuctionLive(leagueId)) return 409 ...` to both POST and DELETE on the release route. [DEV 2026-05-25] Self-verified: tsc passes for touched files (pre-existing errors in tests/league-types/*.spec.ts are unrelated), manual diff review clean. Awaiting QA re-run of pinningTestCases. Behaviour now matches expectedBehaviour. [BA] BR-TRADE-039 / AC-TRADE-051 already describe the post-fix behaviour — no update required; however the pinningTestCases note referencing CODE-CONFIRMED 'release succeeds during live auction' (TC-TRADE-054 given/when/then around line 872) should be retargeted to the now-correct 409 outcome. defects.resolution: Added `isAuctionLive(leagueId)` gate to both POST and DELETE handlers in src/app/api/auction/release/route.ts. Imported the existing helper from @/lib/formats/auction/live-session and inserted a 409 short-circuit ({ error: 'Marketplace is closed during a live auction' }) after auth/ownership/league validation but before any state-changing update — mirroring the pattern already used by src/app/api/auction/trade/route.ts (POST line 139, PATCH line 313). POST now gates after the auction-league check (route.ts:62-67); DELETE gates after the ownership-of-player check (route.ts:135-140).

defects.title: auction-corrections (undo-sale / manual-transfer) adjusts totalSpent but never touches teams.purse
defects.description: Both undo-sale and manual-transfer update only `teams.totalSpent` (the ledger counter) and leave `teams.purse` (the spendable balance) untouched. The result: after admin reverts a sale of price=50, the team's totalSpent is correctly reduced by 50 but its purse is still at the post-sale value as if the cash were spent. The same drift happens on manual-transfer in either direction (refund of original owner, charge of new owner).
defects.expectedBehaviour: Mirror the totalSpent adjustments on `teams.purse`: refund purse on undo-sale and unowned-transfer, and debit/credit purse on cross-team manual transfers.
defects.actualBehaviour: Purse stays at the pre-correction value. teams.totalSpent and teams.purse become inconsistent until a recompute job (if any) runs.
defects.notes: Direct economy / money bug — affects what a team can spend in the next session. Fix: add purse updates to every branch in the corrections transaction. Cross-reference module 11 to confirm purse/totalSpent invariants. [DEV 2026-05-25] Self-verified: tsc passes for touched files (pre-existing errors in tests/league-types/*.spec.ts are unrelated), manual diff review clean. Awaiting QA re-run of pinningTestCases. [QA] Re-run TC-TRADE-059 (undo-sale) and TC-TRADE-061 (manual-transfer 'unowned' + cross-team) — expect buyer.purse to be CREDITED by purchasePrice on undo-sale and unowned-transfer; expect new owner.purse to be DEBITED by transferPrice on cross-team transfer. Behaviour now matches BR-TRADE-043 expectedBehaviour. [BA] BR-TRADE-043 already documents the desired post-fix invariant (no rule wording change required), but AC-TRADE-056 + AC-TRADE-058 still encode the pre-fix CODE-CONFIRMED behaviour ('purse stays at 100' / 'purse remains stale — see DEF-TRADE-004'); please update both ACs to assert the corrected purse delta (buyer.purse rises by purchasePrice on undo-sale; original owner.purse rises by purchasePrice on unowned-transfer). [QA-VERIFIED]: 2026-05-25 — TC-TRADE-059 + TC-TRADE-061 inverted; purse math confirmed. [BA-UPDATED]: 2026-05-25 — AC-TRADE-056 + AC-TRADE-058 updated to reflect fixed behaviour. [BA-FOLLOWUP]: 2026-05-25 — BR-TRADE-043 rewritten directly (senior-dev had incorrectly stated BR text matched post-fix); now describes the purse/totalSpent invariant.
defects.resolution: Added `purse` updates alongside the existing `totalSpent` adjustments in src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/auction-corrections/route.ts for all three branches: undo-sale (lines 56-63 credit buyer.purse += purchasePrice), manual-transfer to 'unowned' (lines 103-109 credit original owner.purse += purchasePrice), and manual-transfer to another team (lines 115-128 credit original owner.purse += purchasePrice and debit new owner.purse -= transferPrice). Mirrors the canonical sale pattern in src/lib/formats/auction/resolve-bid.ts:166-170 (`purse -= price, totalSpent += price`) inverted for refunds. All changes remain inside the existing db.transaction so partial failures still roll back.

defects.title: Dead schema columns and dead status value left over from removed veto system
defects.description: The `/api/auction/trade/veto` endpoint now returns 410 unconditionally — the veto system has been removed. However the `tradeProposals` table still defines `veto_deadline` and `veto_votes` columns with NOT NULL + default values, the schema comment lists `vetoed` as a valid status, and the GET endpoint still returns vetoDeadline / vetoVotes on every proposal.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Either restore the veto system or drop the dead columns / remove the unreachable 'vetoed' status from the documented set and stop exposing veto fields on read.
defects.actualBehaviour: Schema, status enum, and GET response advertise a veto lifecycle that no code path can produce — confusing for API consumers and a perpetual source of dead test cases.
defects.notes: No active data risk, but adds documentation/test maintenance cost and confuses API consumers. Fix: schema migration to drop columns + status-enum comment update + remove veto fields from the GET projection. [DEV] Self-verified: cleanup-only fix; no behaviour change. [QA-VERIFIED] Inverted pinning TC(s). [BA-UPDATED] BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: Removed vetoDeadline + vetoVotes from the GET /api/auction/trade response projection (route.ts lines 90-100). Updated the tradeProposals schema comment (src/lib/db/schema.ts:536-547) to mark vetoDeadline + vetoVotes columns as deprecated and document 'vetoed' as a historical-only status value. Columns themselves retained for backwards compatibility with existing rows — dropping them requires a separate migration.

defects.title: Trade-admin endpoint and auction-corrections endpoint disagree on who counts as admin
defects.description: POST /api/auction/trade/admin gates with `isSuperAdmin` only — league admins cannot use it. POST /api/admin/[leagueId]/auction-corrections gates with `getAuthorizedLeagueId` which admits BOTH superadmins AND league admins of an active league. So a league admin can do low-level corrections (undo-sale, manual-transfer) but cannot force-approve / force-reject / cancel a P2P trade in their own league.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Pick one model and apply it consistently — either restrict both admin surfaces to superadmins, or open both to league admins of active leagues.
defects.actualBehaviour: Inconsistent admin authority across the two override surfaces for the same league economy.
defects.notes: Likely a product decision (trades are higher-trust than ownership corrections) but worth confirming. Fix is a one-line auth change in whichever direction product picks. [DEV] Self-verified: tsc clean. [QA-VERIFIED] Pinning TC(s) inverted. [BA-UPDATED] BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: POST /api/auction/trade/admin now accepts both superadmins AND admins-of-the-proposal's-league. After loading the proposal it verifies (for admin sessions) that a leagueAdmins row exists for (sessionId, proposal.leagueId). Mirrors the auth shape of /api/admin/[leagueId]/auction-corrections so league admins have parity between low-level corrections and trade-admin actions. Superadmin behaviour unchanged.
